sql-schema.note: The schema is Prisma's own schema language, and `prisma migrate dev --schema schema.sql` rejects SQL as invalid schema lines.

check.note: Prisma's schema has no check constraint: `prisma db pull` leaves it out with a warning, and `prisma migrate dev` writes an empty migration.

expression-indexes.note: Prisma's schema has no expression index: `prisma db pull` leaves it out with a warning, and `prisma migrate dev` writes an empty migration.

partial-indexes.note: Only behind the `partialIndexes` preview feature, which `prisma db pull` turns on.

generated-columns.note: Prisma's schema has no computed column: `prisma db pull` writes it as a `dbgenerated` default, which `prisma migrate deploy` fails to run.

domains.note: Prisma's schema has no domain: `prisma db pull` types the column as `Int`, and `prisma migrate dev` adds it as a plain `integer`.

views.note: With the `views` preview feature, `prisma db pull` writes the view, but `prisma migrate dev` writes an empty migration for it.

functions.note: Prisma's schema has no function: `prisma db pull` leaves it out, and `prisma migrate dev` writes an empty migration.

triggers.note: Prisma's schema has no trigger: `prisma db pull` leaves it out, and `prisma migrate dev` writes an empty migration.

rls.note: Prisma's schema has no policy: `prisma db pull` warns that row level security isn't supported, and `prisma migrate dev` writes an empty migration.

extensions.note: Only behind the `postgresqlExtensions` preview feature, and `prisma db pull` leaves the extension out.

renames.note: On a rename, `prisma migrate dev` warns that the column's values will be lost and, once confirmed, writes a drop and an add, so `prisma migrate deploy` empties the column.

view-dependencies.note: For a column a view reads, `prisma migrate dev --create-only` writes a bare `set data type`, which `prisma migrate deploy` cannot run.

non-blocking.note: Prisma writes a plain `create index`, and `@@index` takes no `concurrently` argument.

drift.note: On a database with a hand-added column, `prisma migrate deploy` ran the pending migration without a word, and `prisma migrate status` listed only the pending migration.

out-of-order.note: A merged migration that sorts before one already run was run by `prisma migrate deploy` without a word.

branch-switch.note: After a switch, `prisma migrate dev` reported the other branch's migration as drift and stopped, saying the whole `public` schema must be reset and all its data lost.

lockfile.note: Prisma's `migration_lock.toml` holds only the database provider, so two branches' migrations merged in git without a conflict.

sql-schema.note: The schema is TypeScript: `drizzle-kit generate` finds no schema in a `.sql` file.

domains.note: Drizzle's schema has no domain: `drizzle-kit pull` writes the column as a custom type, and `drizzle-kit migrate` fails because the domain was never created.

functions.note: Drizzle's schema has no function: `drizzle-kit pull` leaves it out, and `drizzle-kit generate` finds no changes.

triggers.note: Drizzle's schema has no trigger: `drizzle-kit pull` leaves it out, and `drizzle-kit generate` finds no changes.

extensions.note: Drizzle's schema has no extension: `drizzle-kit pull` leaves it out, and `drizzle-kit generate` finds no changes.

data-loss.note: The `drizzle-kit push` command asks to confirm the lost data, but `drizzle-kit generate` writes the drop without asking and `drizzle-kit migrate` runs it.

view-dependencies.note: For a column a view reads, `drizzle-kit generate` writes a bare `set data type`, which fails.

non-blocking.note: Drizzle writes a plain `create index`, and its index builder has no `.concurrently()`.

shadow.note: Drizzle writes the migration from snapshots without opening a database, and `drizzle-kit migrate` runs it straight on the target.

drift.note: On a database with a hand-added column, `drizzle-kit migrate` ran the pending migration without a word.

out-of-order.note: A merged migration that sorts before one already run was run by `drizzle-kit migrate` without a word, even when the two migrations end in different schemas in each order.

branch-switch.note: After a switch, `drizzle-kit migrate` left the other branch's table in place unmentioned, and after `drizzle-kit push` removed it, `drizzle-kit migrate` failed with "relation already exists".

lockfile.note: Each migration is a folder of its own, so two branches' migrations merged in git without a conflict.

domains.note: The free standard build refuses domains until `atlas login`, and the community build adds the column without creating its domain.

views.note: The free standard build refuses views until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores them.

functions.note: The free standard build refuses functions until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores them.

triggers.note: The free standard build refuses a trigger's function until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores both.

rls.note: The free standard build refuses policies until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores them.

extensions.note: The free standard build refuses extensions until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores them.

data-loss.note: With `atlas migrate diff`, the drop is written and `atlas migrate apply` runs it without asking, while `atlas schema apply` asks to approve every plan alike.

view-dependencies.note: The free standard build refuses the view until `atlas login`, and the community build's `alter column type` fails on it.

non-blocking.note: Only with `concurrent_index` turned on in `atlas.hcl`; by default `atlas schema apply` writes a plain `create index`.

drift.note: On a database with a hand-added column, the free builds' `atlas migrate apply` ran the pending migration without a word.

branch-switch.note: After a switch, `atlas migrate apply` refused this branch's migration as out of order, or ran it beside the other branch's table, and the community build has no `atlas migrate down`.

open-source.note: The Apache-2.0 community build leaves `atlas migrate down` to the standard build, under Ariga's EULA, and drift alerts to Atlas Pro.

non-blocking.note: It writes a plain `create index`, even for an index declared `concurrently`.

drift.note: Its `apply` refuses a plan whose database changed by hand since it was planned, but it keeps no migration history to deploy.

out-of-order.note: It plans changes only, and keeps no migration history.

branch-switch.note: Its `schema apply` takes the database to this branch's schema and keeps the rest, but it keeps no migrations to rewind.

lockfile.note: It plans changes only, and keeps no migration history.

sql-schema.note: Liquibase's `diff-changelog` compares two live databases, so the target schema has to be built into a second database first.

check.note: For a new or changed check constraint, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes nothing.

partial-indexes.note: For a new partial index, `liquibase diff-changelog` leaves out the `where` clause, so the index covers every row, and it writes nothing when the clause changes.

generated-columns.note: For a new computed column, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes it, but it writes a changed expression as an `addDefaultValue` that `liquibase update` fails to run.

domains.note: For a column of a new domain, `liquibase diff-changelog` adds the column without creating the domain, so `liquibase update` fails.

views.note: On MySQL, `liquibase diff-changelog` copies the view's query with the reference database's name in it, so the view reads the wrong database unless both share a name.

functions.note: For a new or changed function, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes nothing, and it refuses `--diff-types=functions` as an unknown type.

triggers.note: For a new or changed trigger, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes nothing, and it refuses `--diff-types=triggers` as an unknown type.

rls.note: For a new or changed policy, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes nothing, and it refuses `--diff-types=policies` as an unknown type.

extensions.note: For a new extension, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes nothing.

renames.note: On a rename, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes an `addColumn` and a `dropColumn`, and `liquibase update` loses the column's rows.

data-loss.note: Liquibase writes the `dropColumn`, and `liquibase update` runs it without asking.

view-dependencies.note: For a column a view reads, `liquibase diff-changelog` writes a bare `modifyDataType`, which `liquibase update` cannot run.

shadow.note: Liquibase runs the changelog straight on the target, and no command tries it on a throwaway database first.

drift.note: On a database with a hand-added column, `liquibase update` ran the pending changeset without a word.

out-of-order.note: A changeset that sorts before ones already run was run by `liquibase update` without a word.

branch-switch.note: After a switch, `liquibase update` ran this branch's changeset and left the other branch's table in place unmentioned.

open-source.note: Liquibase 5.0.4 ships under the Functional Source License (FSL-1.1-ALv2), which isn't OSI-approved.

drift.note: Flyway Enterprise only: Community refuses `flyway check -drift`, and `flyway migrate` ran the pending migration on a database with a hand-added column without a word.

lockfile.note: Two branches' `V2__…` files merged in git without a conflict, and `flyway migrate` then refused with "Found more than one migration with version 2".

open-source.note: The Apache-2.0 OSS edition has no `diff`, `check` or `undo`, which are in Redgate's editions under its EULA.
